html:
Grameen Bank is a Bangladeshi bank that makes small loans to poor people, nearly all of them women, without asking for collateral. It grew out of a project started in 1976 by Muhammad Yunus, an economics professor at the University of Chittagong, and became a formal bank in 1983. Grameen means village.

Yunus began after the famine of 1974, when he lent a small sum of his own money to women in the village of Jobra who were trapped by moneylenders. Grameen lends to small groups of borrowers who meet every week and back one another, and it reported very high repayment rates.

The model of microcredit spread around the world, and in 2006 Yunus and the bank shared the Nobel Peace Prize. Critics later argued that small loans lift fewer people out of poverty than once claimed. Yunus fell out with Sheikh Hasina, who forced him out of the bank in 2011; in 2024, after she fled the country, he became head of the interim government.
